conventions.axes: Unity axes, metres. Unity x = -Blender x, Unity y = Blender z (up), Unity z = -Blender y. Assumes the kit FBX files are imported with Bake Axis Conversion so each kit object's local axes are Unity axes.
conventions.groups: Pieces that share kit object and material are grouped. Each instance is [object, position, rotation_euler_deg, scale, placement], the KEY POSE (before any motion channel). group.motion lists the same objects in the same order.
conventions.instance.rotation_euler_deg: Unity Euler angles in degrees (Quaternion.Euler(x, y, z)), rounded to 1 degree.
conventions.instance.position: Metres, rounded to 1 mm: the piece's pivot (its base centre, the kit convention; the sword, dagger, funnel and whirl bands, rays and soft rays pivot at their origin: the guard, or the axis foot).
conventions.instance.scale: A number for uniform scale, else [x, y, z] in Unity local axes.
conventions.group.kit_object: The object inside group.kit. A kit of enemy_model means a second skin of the enemy model itself (stone, black) shown over it in the given window; unity_shader_mockup means a shell to build as a shader on the real model.
conventions.group.material: The material the piece wears in the render (shared meshes are re-coloured per piece). Flat emission bands, as pass 2.
conventions.timing: animated. Every piece is keyed at 20 fps; time 0 is frame 7 (frames 1-6 are a 0.3 s lead-in), and each timeline ends with 0.5 s of settle.
conventions.motion: One entry per instance (same order): verb, visible [appear, vanish] s (a vanish of 9 or more means it stays), delay = appear time, duration, easing, and the channels: path = [[t, offset (Unity axes, world-aligned), easing into this key]], scale_keys = [[t, multiplier on the key-pose scale (Unity local x, y, z), easing]], spin = {axis (Unity), keys [[t, degrees, easing]]} applied as Quaternion.AngleAxis(degrees, axis) * keyRotation about the pivot, orbit = {centre (Unity, from the origin), keys [[t, degrees, easing]]} applied last about the vertical through the centre, follow_body = the body index whose motion the piece rides on. Before the first key a channel holds its first value, after the last its last. Easings: linear, out = 1-(1-x)^2, in = x^2, inout = smoothstep, outback = overshoot (c = 1.70158), step = jump at the key. Angles are in Unity's sense.
conventions.bodies: The enemy model (enemy_husk stand-in) per body with its own motion (path, scale_keys, spin, spin2 applied after spin); body 0 is the one the reaction lands on. The stand-ins face the player.
conventions.lights: None: every look is unlit beyond the scene sun.
conventions.ribbons: Curve ribbons (wind curls, lightning arcs, floor combs, chains of light) are not kit meshes: each lists its points (Unity axes, metres, relative to its centre), width_m, radius_profile (taper = thin tail to full head scaled by taper_tail_head; needle = thin at both ends; flat = even), material and ink. Build them as a tube or flat ribbon along the points with the ink outline.

verbs.ribbon_draw: draw_on = [[t, fraction, easing]]: how much is drawn from tail to head (the head leads). erase = [[t, fraction, easing]]: how much is wiped from the tail toward the head. Visible length = draw_on - erase; nothing pops in or out.
verbs.orbit: centre (player, station or body n), radius (m), turns_per_second (Unity sense, + = counter-clockwise from above), start (s), rise (m per s), and optional angle_keys added on top. The ribbon turns about the vertical axis through its centre from start.
verbs.spiral: an orbit with rise > 0: the ribbon climbs while it turns.

conventions.scale: Stand-in enemies are 1.89 m tall, the size of the castle soldiers. Pieces were drawn to read at the game camera (12.7 m); keep their size relative to the body in game, not to the screen.
conventions.source: staging/blender/2026-11-21_strikes/strikes.blend, scene ST, one station per spin look (x from 56000, 40 m apart, in the order earth, ice, fire, water, lightning, metal, life, dark, poison, light, wind). Built by script (spin/tools/spin_specs.py) from the elements 2, 3 and 4 kits, combo kit v3 and the arc strikes kit vfx_strikes_kit.fbx. No new meshes: there is no spin kit file.
conventions.made: 2026-11-21 by Claude through the Blender MCP connection.
conventions.strike_shape: spin: the Scythe's infused strike, attack_scythe_3 (Weapons.cs:145): one full turn (ArcDegrees 360) in its 0.16 s active window, Sweep +1 (from the player's right, round through the front, counter-clockwise seen from above), Reach 3.7 m, best from 2.5 m out (Banded). The effects follow the blade round and break up as they go; never a closed drawn ring (the owner bans rings).
conventions.origin: Every position is relative to the PLAYER's ground point (y = 0), the centre of the turn. Pieces with about_player (placement c) and ribbons whose centre is player are drawn about it; bodies carry their positions from it. Ribbons whose centre is "body k" are relative to that body's ground point. Offsets are world-aligned to the camera. The player faces Unity [-0.643, 0, -0.766] (the station's forward axis) and the turn starts on its right; in game, turn the whole look with the player's facing at the start of the turn.
conventions.spin_timing: The blade passes blade-angle th (0 at the player's right, counter-clockwise) at t = 0.16 * th / 360 s, at a constant speed. Everything on the turn is timed to that pass; blade_pass_s gives the time it passes each struck body. In Unity key them off the swing's own angle, not a fixed delay.
conventions.never_a_ring: Why it never closes: every drawn swirl lies on a spiral (2.35 m from the player where the turn starts, 3.55 m where it would end) and stops 28 degrees short of closing; it is made of separate segments with gaps; each segment is drawn as the blade passes, wiped 0.02 to 0.08 s behind it (at 2,250 degrees a second, so at most about 200 degrees trails the blade), and is carried on round (motion.orbit, degrees about the player) and outward (scale_keys_about_centre: a uniform scale about the player) as it fades. Pieces are spaced unevenly and flung on round and outward. Keep all of these in Unity.
conventions.instance.placement: g = on the ground, b = on or around a body, c = about the player (the centre of the turn).
conventions.carrier: The grey stand-in scythe in the renders (stk_scythe, role ref, a 3.75 m haft with a 1.1 m blade at hip height) is a mock-up of the turn only: it is not in this recipe and nothing is drawn on the weapon.
conventions.motion.body: The body (index into bodies) a piece belongs to, with about_body = its position from that body (Unity axes). Written from the pass's specs (spin/tools/spin_specs.py) by spin/tools/spin_assemble_recipe.py.
conventions.per_struck_enemy: motion.per_struck_enemy = true marks a piece that exists once for each enemy the turn actually hits, placed about_body from that enemy and timed from the moment the blade passes it; spawn one set per struck enemy and none on a miss. Bodies 0 to 3 are inside the reach (struck_bodies); body 4 is outside it (missed_bodies) and has nothing drawn on it.
conventions.look_fields: Each look carries element, moment (infused), strike_shape (spin), weapon, owner, answer, look (in words), struck_bodies, missed_bodies, blade_pass_s and per_struck_enemy_pieces.
conventions.dark_outline: Dark's hands (vfxst_hand_big_open, vfxst_hand_big_grip: one rounded organic mesh each; material st_hand_small, near-black with a violet rim) were rendered with a violet outline on their outer silhouette (Freestyle line set InkHands, colour 0.42, 0.18, 0.7 linear, thickness 1.5). Each hand is one merged mesh, so the outline never traces joins between parts. In Unity give them an outline pass in that colour on the silhouette only. The spin's shadow wisps (vfxe2_cloud_a/_b in st_sl_shadow_smoke) take the same violet silhouette outline.
conventions.poison_veins: Poison's bruise, wound, vein web and sheen are ribbons whose points were snapped onto the stand-in body's surface and sunk into it so they lie flat on the skin (the bruise shows as a flat patch about 1.5 cm proud, the fine vessels as painted lines) and ride its motion (follow_body). In Unity build them as a decal or a vein and bruise mask in the enemy's shader that spreads from the wound with the same timing; nothing should stand out of the body.
conventions.colour: Materials are flat emission in linear colour (ramp ones shade by facing, centre to rim), except the toon stone, which is lit toon with the ink outline. Poison uses the slam's st_sl_venom (near-black green with a sickly-green rim) so it reads on dark floors. No stop reaches pure white: the strip maker counts pure-white pixels in every strip frame (spin/white_check.json): every look is 0.
